hints: Look closely at what the apparatus actually does, vapour from gentle heat is passed over a strongly heated solid then a gas is collected over water.
Recall that hot alumina or silica acts as a heterogeneous catalyst for elimination and for breaking long chains, not as an oxidising agent.
Check which of the three named processes gives an insoluble gaseous alkene product and which one would need a liquid oxidiser and different apparatus.
walkthrough:
**Read the apparatus like a story**

Gentle heat vaporises liquid X on the mineral wool. The vapour then passes over strongly heated silica, alumina or baked clay. Finally a gas that does not dissolve much in water is collected.

This tells you it is a gas-phase reaction over a hot porous solid catalyst.

**Test process 2, dehydration of ethanol**

Hot alumina is the classic catalyst for dehydration of an alcohol to an alkene:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH(g)} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(g)}$$
Ethene is insoluble in water, so it can be collected over water. This fits perfectly, so 2 is correct.

**Test process 3, cracking of paraffin**

Cracking breaks a long alkane vapour into a shorter alkane plus an alkene using strong heat and a silica or alumina catalyst:
$$\text{long alkane} \rightarrow \text{shorter alkane} + \text{alkene}$$
For example, $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{22} \rightarrow \text{C}_8\text{H}_{18} + \text{C}_2\text{H}_4$. The alkene products are gases collected over water. This also fits perfectly, so 3 is correct.

**Test process 1, oxidation of ethanol**

Oxidation of ethanol to ethanal or ethanoic acid needs a chemical oxidising agent, typically heated acidified potassium dichromate(VI):
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
There is no oxidiser here, only inert porous solids, and the products are liquids, not gases for collection over water. Heating is normally under reflux or gentle distillation, not passing vapour over a red-hot solid. So 1 cannot be demonstrated, leaving 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes process 1. Oxidation needs acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ or similar oxidiser and gives liquid products. The hot silica/alumina set-up provides no oxygen source and collects a gas, so 1 does not fit.
options.B: Incorrect because any combination containing 1 is wrong. Students sometimes think strong heat alone oxidises ethanol in air, but controlled oxidation to ethanal or ethanoic acid requires a specific oxidising agent and different apparatus.
options.C: Correct because both 2 and 3 fit. Dehydration of ethanol vapour over hot alumina gives ethene gas, and cracking of paraffin vapour over hot silica/alumina gives smaller alkenes, both insoluble gases collectable over water.
options.D: Incorrect because process 1 alone is impossible here. This trap comes from confusing heating an alcohol with oxidising it. Without dichromate or manganate, no oxidation to $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ occurs.
